full_judgment: 3. The Election Tribunal did not utter a word as to what parties' evidence was with regard to the material allegations of the opposite party No. 1. The evidence of 6 PWs and 5 OPWs were left completely untouched by the Election Tribunal. The Tribunal opened the ballot boxes in presence of the learned Advocates of the petitioner and the opposite-party No. 1 and recounted the same. It found that in the polling station of Ward No. 3, i.e. Datra Primary School Polling Centre the petitioner obtained 780 votes. The Returning Officer had shown that the petitioner had obtained 12222 votes in this centre. The difference is of 442 votes. The Tribunal also recounted the ballot papers of the Union Parishad Members of the Datra Centre. The same number of ballot books and ballot papers were found to have been used and cast as those of the candidates for Chairmanship. In the election of Chairman and Members, 8 ballot books were found to have been used in full and only one book was partly used. The Tribunal found it impossible that out of 1414 total votes at Ward No. 3, the petitioner could have secured 1222 votes. From the recounting it drew the "presumption" that the petitioner had made a new polling station at Datra with a view to exercising undue influence over the voters.
